Diagnosis:
The failing test `isUnixSymlinkIsFalseIfMoreThanOneFlagIsSet` checks if the method `isUnixSymlink()` returns false for a Zip entry called "META-INF/maven/". This entry is expected not to be a Unix symbolic link.

Looking at the implementation of the `isUnixSymlink()` method in `ZipArchiveEntry`, it determines whether an entry is a Unix symlink by examining the Unix mode bits. It checks if the `LINK_FLAG` bit is set in the Unix mode:

```java
public boolean isUnixSymlink() {
    return (getUnixMode() & UnixStat.LINK_FLAG) == UnixStat.LINK_FLAG;
}
```

`LINK_FLAG` is defined as octal 0120000, which corresponds to the Unix file type bitfield for symbolic links.

`getUnixMode()` returns the stored Unix mode bits if the platform is UNIX; otherwise, it returns zero.

The current bug report mentions that `isUnixSymlink` erroneously returns true for entries with Unix permissions 177777, which is an unusual mode containing more than one flag set. This suggests that the current check:

```java
(getUnixMode() & LINK_FLAG) == LINK_FLAG
```

can return true even if other bits (besides the symlink flag) are set because it only checks if the symlink bit is present.

The failing test expects `isUnixSymlink` to be false when more than one flag (mode bit) is set; i.e., it expects stricter checking that the mode matches exactly the symlink flag, not just that the flag is present.

Hence, the bug is that `isUnixSymlink()` only tests if the symlink flag bit is set, rather than that it is the only relevant flag set, allowing cases where other unrelated bits are set to also report true incorrectly. This matches the behavior seen in the test and the bug report.

Recent bug reports do not appear related to this area; the evidence from the method implementations and test names directly explains the failure.

The root cause is that the `isUnixSymlink()` logic only does a bitwise AND check for the presence of the symlink bit, instead of checking that the mode precisely indicates a symlink (with no other bits set that would invalidate this).

The fix should involve changing `isUnixSymlink()` to verify the full mode matches exactly the symlink type bits, rather than just testing the presence of the symlink bit flag.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
